analysis: What changed versus the 5:00 AM brief: the CPI print landed hot and flipped the tape. Headline CPI rose 0.4% (vs 0.3% expected) and core 0.3% (vs 0.2%), the third straight 0.3% core reading — and that 0.3% is exactly the level Waller said pre-release would justify considering a 50bp December hike, so the half-point scenario is now live in the debate even though no official has endorsed it post-print. Futures went from flat-to-mixed (S&P +0.01%, Nasdaq-100 -0.39% at 7:13 AM ET) to lower (S&P -0.3%, Nasdaq-100 -0.8%, Dow +0.1%) after the 8:30 AM ET release, with the Nasdaq hit hardest — the classic rate-sensitive leg. Nvidia's early +1.3% premarket bounce has fully reversed to -1.66% ($175.70 at 8:57 AM ET); the governance discount is still in charge a week after the 11.58% five-session slide, and the House reply deadline is tomorrow. The megacaps mostly gave back a slice of Monday's gains (TSLA -1.83%, AMZN -0.62%, MSFT -0.42%, META -0.38%, GOOGL -0.15%) with Apple the lone gainer (+0.48%) — a pause, not a reversal, of Monday's +2.4-5.5% moves. Oil deepened its slide (Brent below $90, WTI below $85), which is the one disinflationary offset in the print and keeps energy under pressure. Anthropic's IPO filing (800M+ shares at $70-78, valuation above $1T) prices AI's biggest private name into public markets amid the AI-valuation wobble. Signal vs noise: the hot core print and the 50bp question are the signal; the WSB mood overnight ('CPI pumps no matter what') is noise — futures are lower, not higher. Sea's mixed print and Hims' guide cut are carried context, not fresh drivers. What matters into the open is whether the Dow's resilience (still +0.1%) holds while tech digests the rate repricing, and whether CoreWeave's after-close print steadies the neocloud/AI-infrastructure tape.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: October CPI came in hot: headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% expected) and core CPI rose 0.3% (vs +0.2% expected), the third straight 0.3% core reading. Shelter rose 0.3% and accounted for over 30% of the monthly increase; food +0.5%, energy +0.7%. No official year-over-year rate was published because BLS never collected October 2025 prices during last year's shutdown; economists had estimated ~3.9% headline.
headlines.why_it_matters: Both readings beat consensus by 0.1 point, so the disinflation story stalled — and a 0.3% core print is exactly the level Waller flagged for considering a bigger December hike.

headlines.headline: October core CPI hit Waller's threshold for considering a half-point December hike: in his London speech hours before the release, Fed Governor Waller said a 50bp move 'should be considered' if core CPI rose 0.3% or more — and it printed 0.3%. That is his pre-release condition being met, not a new post-release call, and the decision remains the FOMC's. Traders still see a quarter-point December hike as near-certain per CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: The 50bp scenario is now live in the debate rather than hypothetical — that repricing is why rate-sensitive tech, not the Dow, is leading futures lower.

headlines.headline: Futures turned lower after the CPI release: S&P 500 futures -0.3%, Nasdaq-100 futures -0.8% and Dow futures +0.1% into the open, versus +0.01% / -0.39% / +0.37% at 7:13 AM ET before the print. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.9%, up slightly from last night.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape flipped from a quiet hold of Monday's rally to a rate-driven tech selloff in one print — the Nasdaq's -0.8% shows where the hike repricing bites hardest.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's early premarket bounce fully reversed: after rising ~1.3% early on the Trump 'I believe him' comment about CEO Jensen Huang, NVDA was -1.66% premarket ($175.70 at 8:57 AM ET) and the most active premarket name. The board probe has no published timeline; Huang's reply to the House chairmen is due tomorrow, Nov 11, ahead of a Nov 18 closed-door briefing. NVDA reports Q3 earnings Nov 17.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce fading into a fresh decline despite analyst support (Mizuho $250 target, Goldman Buy, Bernstein Outperform) shows the stock is still trading the investigation timeline, not fundamentals, a week after falling 11.58% in five sessions.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mostly lower in premarket after the hot print: as of ~8:57-8:59 AM ET, TSLA -1.83% ($371.14), AMZN -0.62% ($265.26), MSFT -0.42% ($542.88), META -0.38% ($638.94) and GOOGL -0.15% ($287.73), while AAPL is the lone gainer at +0.48% ($352.36). All six gained 1.2-5.5% in Monday's rally.
headlines.why_it_matters: A modest give-back of Monday's gains rather than a rout — the group is digesting the rate repricing, with Tesla the softest after its +5.54% Monday.

headlines.headline: Anthropic's IPO is moving forward: the Claude maker said in a regulatory filing it plans to sell more than 800 million shares, with shareholders selling another 25 million, at an expected $70-78 per share — an implied valuation above $1 trillion, which would make it one of the biggest publicly traded U.S. companies on arrival, though some investors had expected as much as twice that earlier this year.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest private AI name is pricing into public markets right in the middle of the AI-valuation wobble — a test of whether appetite for AI paper survives the rate repricing.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave shares were down about 2% premarket ahead of Q3 results after today's close. Analysts expect $162 million in net income on $1.3 billion in revenue, per Visible Alpha. D-Wave Quantum and Rigetti also report after the bell.
headlines.why_it_matters: The neocloud demand-and-debt test lands tonight — after investors ditched the shares over financial-health concerns, the print decides whether the AI-infrastructure tape steadies or extends its slide.

headlines.headline: Oil's slide deepened: Brent fell about 3% to $89.88 a barrel and WTI fell more than 2% to below $85, after Brent slipped below $90 for the first time since August. President Trump said military action against Iran was not needed 'at this point'. Gold prices were slipping and bitcoin was holding above $74,000.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cheaper crude is the one disinflationary offset inside a hot CPI print — it trims the inflation impulse even as it keeps energy names under pressure.

headlines.headline: Rocket Lab stayed under pressure in premarket after reporting a wider Q3 net loss, despite record revenue of $267.8M and a $3.57B backlog. RKLB had gained 10.9% on Monday and was one of the most-mentioned tickers on r/wallstreetbets in the last 24 hours.
headlines.why_it_matters: Record revenue with a wider loss is the growth-vs-profitability tension in miniature — the backlog is the offset, but the market is punishing the loss line first.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carried forward: record Q3 reported Nov 3 (revenue $357.2M, +43% YoY vs ~$348.32M consensus; Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M; DCF coverage 1.67x; EPS $0.33, in line), the $0.525 per-unit distribution paid Fri Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26, and full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. Call color: over 60% of new horsepower scheduled for 2027 delivery is contracted (~90% of first-half deliveries); ~$500M order book through 2029; utilization slipped to 92.1% from 94.0%. New filing note: Alps Advisors raised its stake 15.5% in Q3 and now owns ~14.55% of the partnership. Management flagged cost pressure — monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 ~25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September. Cross-current today: oil's slide deepened (WTI below $85, Brent $89.88) and pressures energy names broadly, though USAC's compression business is fee-based.
